climate.tropical.about: Warm in every month and no frost; the year turns on wet and dry seasons.
climate.subtropical.about: Hot, humid summers and mild winters with little frost, or mild highlands with a dry winter.
climate.mediterranean.about: Dry, warm to hot summers and mild, rainy winters.
climate.arid.about: Little rain, far less than the sun and wind dry out: deserts and steppes, hot or cold.
climate.temperate.about: Mild all year, with rain in every season, cool summers and light frosts.
climate.continental.about: Cold winters with lasting frost or snow, and warm to hot summers.
climate.boreal.about: Long, very cold winters and short, cool summers.
climate.title: What is your climate?
climate.lede: Pages that change with the climate show yours first and hide nothing. Your choice stays on this device.
home.consortium.lede: A consortium is a group of plants that help each other. Choose your climate: start from a suggestion of 6 to 12 plants, or build your own, up to hundreds.
home.consortium.note: A beta with three climates so far: tropical, Mediterranean and temperate.
consortium.title: Design a consortium
consortium.description: Choose your climate: start from a suggestion of 6 to 12 plants, or build your own, up to hundreds. A free beta tool from Canopi.

consortium.region.southern_america: Central and South America and the Caribbean
consortium.job.feeds_you.about: Fruit, roots, leaves or seeds you can eat.
consortium.job.feeds_soil.about: Takes nitrogen from the air with bacteria on its roots. When it is cut back and its leaves rot, the plants around it need less feeding.
consortium.job.mulch.about: Grows fast and takes cutting back; the cuttings cover and feed the soil. Deep roots bring up minerals.
consortium.job.ground.about: Keeps the soil shaded, moist and alive, and keeps weeds down.
consortium.job.helpers.about: Flowers that feed bees and the insects that eat pests.
consortium.job.shelter.about: Breaks the wind, repels or traps pests, or gives birds and other wildlife a home.

what.title: From a blank map to a planting plan
what.lede: Everything happens on the real map of your land.
what.map.title: Draw on your land
what.map.text: Find your site, outline it with zones, then place plants one by one or in rows. Measure and annotate over the map, satellite imagery or contours.
what.map.alt: Canopi with an example food forest on the map of Central Park, New York: planting belts in rings around a pond, with the tools around the map.
what.catalog.title: Find the right plants
what.catalog.text: Search {count} species by common or scientific name, filter them, and keep your favourites, in 11 languages.
what.catalog.alt: The plant catalog panel: a search box, filters and a list of species.
what.plan.title: Plan the work and the cost
what.plan.text: Schedule actions on a calendar, price each species in a budget, and see strata and succession in the consortium view.
what.plan.alt: The calendar panel: a month view and the planting actions scheduled for November.
what.export: When it’s ready, take it to the field: a planting-plan PDF with field sheets, GeoJSON, or your own .canopi file.

consortium.future.title: Future climate
consortium.future.lede: Each plant is checked against your site’s projected climate, at the latest period it grows into: 2041–2070, or 2071–2099 for climax plants. The projections add the changes of a constrained CMIP6 model ensemble (Beck et al., 2023) to the CHELSA v2.1 climate of 1981–2010. Each range is where the plant is recorded, cultivation included. Estimates, not reviewed.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: What projectcanopi.com receives, what stays on your device, and which other services are contacted, and when.
privacy.site.title: Visiting the site
privacy.site.host: Canopi is a non-profit association under French law. Cloudflare hosts the site: like any web host, it receives each request your browser makes to projectcanopi.com, with your IP address. Requests that run the site’s own code, such as sending a form, are recorded in Cloudflare’s logs with the request’s details: the address requested, the time, your browser and an approximate location (such as city, country and network). The site’s code never logs what you wrote.
privacy.site.none: There is no account, no analytics and no advertising, and the site’s own code sets no cookies.
privacy.site.storage: Your browser keeps a few settings on this device: the light or dark theme, the climate you chose, the ticks in a guide’s checklists and, for this visit only, the fact that it already offered your language.
privacy.site.logs: Cloudflare keeps these logs for up to 7 days: {link}
privacy.tool.title: The consortium tool
privacy.tool.device: The tool runs in your browser. It downloads the plant list and the climate files from projectcanopi.com, and keeps your consortium, your country and your site’s climate on this device, in the browser’s local storage. None of it is sent to Canopi.
privacy.tool.share: A share link holds your consortium after the # of the address, a part browsers never send to a server: only the people you give the link to can see it.
privacy.location.title: Your site’s location
privacy.location.device: If you let the tool use your device’s location, your browser asks your permission first. The location is used on your device to read the climate and the country, and saved only on this device.
privacy.location.tiles: To read the climate, your browser downloads whole files from projectcanopi.com, each covering about 1,000 km, so these downloads do not reveal the precise point. If you open the map, OpenFreeMap receives the area it shows; a place search sends the text you typed to Nominatim (see below).
privacy.location.link: A share link includes your location only if you tick the box to include it, and then only as its grid cell, about 11 km across, and its country.
privacy.location.search: Place search: when you press Enter, the text you typed goes to Nominatim, run by the OpenStreetMap Foundation, with what any website receives (your IP address, browser and language). Type a town or village, not your address.
privacy.location.map: Map: OpenFreeMap sends the map’s tiles and styles only once you open the map. It receives your IP address and the area the map shows.
privacy.contact.title: The contact form
privacy.contact.body: The contact form sends your name, your email address, your message and the page’s language to Canopi by email: Cloudflare delivers it to Canopi’s mailbox at Gmail (Google). They are used only to reply to you, and the site keeps no copy.
privacy.correction.title: Suggesting a correction
privacy.correction.body: In the consortium tool, the correction form sends the plant, the value it shows, your suggestion and your note, the data release, the climate and the page’s language to Canopi by email, the same way. Before sending, you agree that your suggestion may be published in Canopi’s plant data under CC BY-SA 4.0.
privacy.correction.email: Your email address is optional: if you give it, it is used only to reply to you and is never published.
privacy.donate.title: Donations
privacy.donate.body: The donation form belongs to HelloAsso, a French payment platform for associations. It loads only when you open the donation window, and what you enter there goes to HelloAsso, under its own privacy policy.
privacy.ask.title: Questions
privacy.ask.body: To ask what Canopi holds about you, or to have a message deleted, write to us through the {link}.
dataSources.tool.title: The consortium tool: climate, places and maps
dataSources.tool.lede: The consortium tool reads your site’s climate and country from the canopi-climate grid, and the plants’ observed climate ranges from GBIF. Names, citations and licences appear as their sources publish them.
dataSources.tool.gridUse: Your site’s climate and country, read on your device.
dataSources.tool.servedUse: Served with the grid; the tool does not use it yet.
dataSources.tool.gbifUse: The plants’ observed climate ranges come from these maps, cultivated plants included. A GBIF derived-dataset DOI will be added here once it is registered.
dataSources.tool.mapUse: The map for choosing your site, loaded only when you open it.
dataSources.tool.searchUse: The place search, used only when you press Enter.
dataSources.tool.privacy: What the map and the place search receive: {link}.
